source_text: Sicut in novissimis diebus Verbum Dei ex Maria carne vestitum processit — aliud quod videbatur, aliud quod intelligebatur — ita cum per prophetas vel legislatorem Verbum profertur, litterae velamine tegitur. Levitici ritus et hostiae littera tamquam caro sunt; spiritalis sensus tamquam divinitas. Beati oculi qui velamine litterae obtectum Spiritum vident. Sequentes solam historiam ad vitulos et agnos offerendos coguntur; ecclesia Susannae vocibus utitur: melius est in manus vestras incidere quam peccare in Domino. Conversis ad Dominum aufertur velamen; ubi Spiritus Domini, ibi libertas. Revela oculos meos, et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua.
thought_title: The letter as flesh, the spiritual sense as divinity
orientation: Origen opens the homily by explaining how the Word of God comes veiled in the letter of Leviticus, just as Christ came veiled in flesh from Mary.
pass_a_gloss: Just as in [the] last days [the] Word of God from Mary with flesh clothed went forth — one thing which was being seen, another thing which was being understood — so when through prophets or [the] lawgiver [the] Word is brought forth, with [the] veil of [the] letter it is covered. Of Leviticus [the] rites and sacrifices [the] letter as if flesh are; [the] spiritual sense as if divinity. Blessed [are the] eyes which [the] Spirit covered with [the] veil of [the] letter see. [Those] following only [the] history to calves and lambs to be offered are compelled; [the] church [the] words of Susanna uses: better it is into your hands to fall than to sin against [the] Lord. [To those] turned to [the] Lord is taken away [the] veil; where [the] Spirit of [the] Lord [is], there [is] freedom. Reveal my eyes, and I will consider [the] wonders of your law.

choices.why: Keeps the clothing metaphor explicit, matching the veil imagery that follows.

choices.english: is covered with the veil of the letter
choices.why: Preserves the passive construction and the instrumental sense of velamine.

choices.english: the spiritual sense is as divinity
choices.why: Keeps the compressed comparison without adding a verb, matching the Latin parallelism.
rejected: the spiritual sense is like the divine nature

choices.why: Echoes the beatitude form, which Origen deliberately evokes.

choices.term: melius est in manus vestras incidere quam peccare in Domino
choices.english: it is better to fall into your hands than to sin against the Lord
choices.why: Renders the Susanna quotation literally, preserving the comparative structure and the phrase 'in Domino'.
rejected: better to fall into your hands than to sin before the Lord
it is better to be in your hands than to sin in the Lord

choices.english: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom
choices.why: Keeps the terse Pauline formula without adding a copula where the Latin omits it.
rejected: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty
wherever the Lord's Spirit is, there is freedom

pass_b_english: Just as in the last days the Word of God came forth from Mary clothed in flesh—one thing was seen, another was understood—so when the Word is brought forth through the prophets or the lawgiver, it is covered with the veil of the letter. The rites and sacrifices of Leviticus are as flesh in the letter; the spiritual sense is as divinity. Blessed are the eyes that see the Spirit hidden beneath the veil of the letter. Those who follow only the history are compelled to offer calves and lambs; the church uses the words of Susanna: it is better to fall into your hands than to sin against the Lord (Susanna 1:23). For those converted to the Lord the veil is taken away (2 Corinthians 3:16); where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom (2 Corinthians 3:17). Reveal my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law (Psalm 119:18).

last_rejected.source_quote: Revela oculos meos, et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua
last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 118:18, not Hebrew 119:18; LXX numbering is one behind Hebrew for Psalms 10-148.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 119:18 is standard English Bible numbering; acceptable for English readers despite LXX difference.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'Revela' means 'uncover/open', not 'reveal'; biblical idiom is 'Open my eyes'.
last_rejected.fix: Open my eyes, and I will behold the wonders of your law
last_rejected.ruling: 'Revela' = 'uncover/open'; 'reveal my eyes' conveys this adequately; not a meaning-changing error.
